rv.q: Terry Johnson's production is a tremendous, if painful, tribute to Garland.

But, for all the skill of the acting and the smoothness of Terry Johnson's production, it's hard to love a play that invites us to wallow in Garland's tragic decline without offering much in the way of enlightenment.

The show is a virtual reincarnation of the last difficult months of her life as she struggles to fulfil a five-week engagement at London’s Talk Of The Town egged on by her latest flame, a toyboy fiancé who became her last husband just three months before she died.

cn.t: Critics are divided on the bio-play itself, but united in praise for Tracie Bennett's stunning, harrowing performance as Judy Garland—a tour-de-force turn that elevates familiar material into must-see theatre.
